about: The “Líbera nos” develops the final petition of the Lord's Prayer: “deliver us from evil”. It asks that deliverance through the intercession of the Virgin Mary, the Apostles Peter, Paul and Andrew, and all the saints. The priest says it secretly over the paten and signs himself with it, and only the closing Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum is heard.

s01.narrative: The priest takes the paten in his right hand, between the forefinger and the middle finger, holds it upright over the altar, and says the prayer silently.

s02.translation: Deliver us, Lord, we pray, from every evil, past, present and to come: and by the intercession of the blessed and glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of God, with Your blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and Andrew, and all the Saints,

s03.narrative: The priest signs himself with the paten, from forehead to breast.

s04.translation: graciously grant peace in our days,

s06.translation: that, by the help of Your mercy, we may be always free from sin and safe from all distress.

s07.narrative: The priest slips the paten under the Host, uncovers the chalice, genuflects, rises, takes the Host, and holding it over the chalice with both hands breaks it in two.

s08.translation: Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord, Your Son.

s09.narrative: The priest lays the half held in his right hand on the paten and breaks a small particle from the half remaining in his left.

s10.translation: Who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God.

s11.narrative: The priest joins the other half to the half on the paten, holds the small particle over the chalice, and says in an audible voice or sings:

w001.function: A second-person singular imperative opening the prayer.

w008.function: The first of three ablative plural adjectives agreeing with “malis” (w007).

w013.function: A participle forming an ablative absolute with “Vírgine” (w018).

w033.function: An adjective used as a noun: the holy ones.

w035.function: A nominative adjective agreeing with the understood subject of “da” (w034).

w040.function: It introduces a purpose clause with “simus” (w048) as its verb.

w044.function: A participle agreeing with the understood subject of “simus” (w048).

w045.function: The first half of an et… et… pair with “et” (w051): both free from sin and safe from disquiet.

w048.function: The verb of the clause introduced by “ut” (w040), with “líberi” (w050) and “secúri” (w055) as predicates.

w065.function: The preposition “cum” is attached to the end of the pronoun “te”.

w073.function: Nominative referring to the subject of “vivit” (w066) and “regnat” (w068).
